1999.label: NBA Live 99
1999.name: The NLSC
1999.terms: 'NBA Live 99 Original 1998 Rosters' 1.0 (8 March 2017, uploaded by Andrew) from the NLSC's Downloads database: EA's own roster files from the NBA Live 99 PC CD-ROM (© EA Sports 1998), no licence given. The .7z (MD5 6280cd1d87748d80689c053037c028e0) is pinned as downloaded, and its PLAYERS.DBF and TEAMS.DBF as extracted; only those two dBase tables are read, as data. Because of the 1998 lockout the game shipped with the final 1997/98 rosters plus the trades of May and June 1998 and none of the 1998 draft; the season is 1998/99, the edition's, as NBA 2K12 carries 2011/12 on the lockout's 2010/11 rosters. Free agents and the All-Star teams are left out, and so is every player Basketball-Reference (check) does not have playing in the NBA: the made-up 'Roster Player' and a draft pick who never played. Each player keeps EA's computed overall (OVERALLRTG) as `raw`, put on NBA 2K's scale by `scale`.

scale.note: NBA Live 99's overall is the rounded mean of 17 of its ratings, so it runs low (28-71 here) and undervalues specialists. One straight line puts it on NBA 2K's scale: the least-squares line of NBA 2K's overall (2K Archive's NBA 2K, 1999/00) on NBA Live 99's, through the players both editions rate, matched by name or alias. rating = round(20.22 + 1.089 × raw); its slope is positive, so no player passes another. The build fits the line again and stops if it is not this one. The audit gives every raw overall's rating and how the line does on those players.

computed.label: Basketball-Reference (computed)
computed.name: Sumitro Datta, NBA Stats (1947-present), Kaggle, CC0, version 57
computed.terms: CC0: Public Domain (Kaggle's metadata), Sumitro Datta's copy of Basketball-Reference's regular seasons, dataset version 57 (updated 1 November 2026), downloaded anonymously from Kaggle's API; nothing was fetched from basketball-reference.com. PER, WS/48 and defensive win shares are Basketball-Reference's own calculations; Sports-Reference's data-use terms forbid scraping that harms its sites, building a competing database and AI training with its data, and say facts are not copyrightable. Advanced.csv gives each player season's position, games, minutes, PER, WS/48 and DWS; Player Totals.csv points, rebounds and assists (the same file `check` pins); All-Star Selections.csv and End of Season Teams.csv the All-Star and All-NBA picks; Player Career Info.csv the career position (G, F-C...), for a player a season lists no position for and for a second position his other seasons do not give; Team Summaries.csv each team's name (checked against `teams`), SRS (the audit's comparison only) and the league's pace and offensive rating, and Team Stats Per Game.csv its points a game (both checked against src/data/nbaLeagueAverages.js).

score.note: score = intercept + the sum of each coefficient times its input: PER and WS/48 shrunk toward a bench player's 11 and 0.05 by 400 minutes ((value × minutes + prior × 400) / (minutes + 400)), minutes a game and its square, points, rebounds and assists a game, All-Star (1 if picked), All-NBA (3, 2 or 1 for the 1st, 2nd or 3rd team) and defensive win shares, from the player's whole season. The coefficients are the least-squares fit of NBA 2K's overall, as a z-score within each edition, on those inputs from each player's season before (2K rates a season's players from the season before), over 2K Archive's NBA 2K (1999/00) to NBA 2K26 (2025/26), its NBA 2K12 its own, players matched by name (and club where two share one): 9,970 pairs. Every coefficient is positive. The build fits them again and stops if any differs at six significant figures; the ratings use these, so a later copy of 2K Archive's page cannot move them.

computed.rule: Each season, each club's 13 players with the most minutes are rated (a traded player counts once, for the club he played the most minutes for). The league is ranked by score, and the player at rank quantile (rank - 0.5) / N takes NBA 2K27's rating at that quantile of its ratings of each club's 13 best (2K Archive, 390 ratings from 69 to 97, `spread.counts`; the build stops if the page's differ): no player passes another. A player's positions are the season's, else the first his career position implies (`positions`); the second is the neighbouring one he was listed at in other seasons with the most minutes, else the one his career position implies. A player with no position is left out. No input is a team's result (no SRS, record or point margin), though Basketball-Reference's defensive win shares, and so WS/48, start from each club's points allowed.
